observations.body: Paul receives the Philippians’ renewed support, says he has learned contentment, and calls their gifts a fragrant, acceptable sacrifice pleasing to God.
observations.label: A financial gift becomes fragrant sacrifice

observations.body: The passage presents material support, contentment, partnership, received gift, aroma, acceptance, and divine supply as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: material support, contentment, partnership, received gift, aroma, acceptance, and divine supply

observations.body: The passage places gift as sacrifice beside material support, contentment, partnership, received gift, aroma, acceptance, and divine supply.
observations.label: gift as sacrifice

payload.posture: Read Philippians 4:10–20 as evidence about sacrifice, keeping its action, claim, context, and limits distinct.
payload.tension: the sacrificial metaphor honors concrete generosity rather than replacing it with words alone
payload.title: A financial gift becomes fragrant sacrifice
